summary: Microbatch rate-ladder mismatch on tiered dedicated conversion causing missing burst credits
description: Issue summary: Customer converted from self-serve hosted plan to a tiered Dedicated contract on 2026-03-09. Post-conversion invoices and provisional credits show missing burst/microbatch credits for several hourly windows during the first full day of dedicated routing. Impact: Customer reports a $12.3K provisional overcharge on the 03/10 provisional invoice and is requesting immediate reconciliation and provisional credit. Environment: prod-us-west dedicated pool, conversion happened during regional cutover, requests routed via fallback to hosted briefly. Suspected domains: rate ladder evaluation, postback filtering, and dedicated fallback tagging. Customer impact: billing overage alert triggered, finance review paused autosettle for the cycle.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer switched to Dedicated plan and pinned reserved capacity on 2026-03-09 at 22:00 UTC
2) Multiple asynchronous microbatch jobs (embedding batching and small chat bursts) ran between 2026-03-10 00:00-04:00 UTC
3) Postbacks from edge/ingesters include dedup and filtering metadata; some postbacks marked as fallback-hosted during short capacity reconciliation
4) Billing reconciler applied tiered rate-ladder lookup and assigned microbatch tariff bucket, expected to credit burst buffer — but provisional invoice shows no burst credit for affected hours

comments: 2026-03-12 - Aisha Patel (Support): Opened ticket after customer attachment of provisional invoice and CSV of usage windows. Noted that several microbatch windows show zero burst credits despite >50% burst utilization.
2026-03-12 - Evan Morales (Billing Eng): Investigating if rate-ladder resolution used stale plan mapping during the conversion window. Asking for postback traces and tenant mapping snapshot.
2026-03-13 - Customer (InSight Analytics - Jenna Li): Confirming they saw a change in invoice lines and attached 03-10 provisional. Urgent: finance has hold on payment until resolved.

2026-03-13 - Evan Morales (Billing Eng): Found evidence that some postbacks were classified as fallback-hosted while tenant was already in dedicated pool; raised hypothesis that a race during cutover caused rate-service to fallback to hosted tag before reserved-tag propagation completed.

2026-03-14 - SRE (Marcus Green): Ran a targeted re-ingest of queued postbacks for tenant insight-acc-78; 987 postbacks reprocessed and mapped to dedicated ladder bucket. Awaiting billing rerun to confirm credit application.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Race condition during dedicated pool registration -> rate-service returned hosted tariff for first write, so billing never applied dedicated burst credits for those hours.
Hypothesis B: Postback filter logic dropped 'reserved=true' tag on some microbatch lines when fallback routing occurred; reconciler then used fallback-hosted flags to suppress credits.

Partial finding: rateservice logs show ladder_bucket changed from microbatch-50 to hosted-normal for ~14% of sequences in the 00:00-04:00 UTC window. Postback-ingester shows out-of-order queueing and one transient error that aligns with cutover timing.
Customer provided CSV correlates 00:10-00:45 and 02:12-02:32 windows where invoicing differs; these windows match postback gaps in ingester traces.
resolution: Mitigation completed 2026-03-14: Manual reprocessing of affected postbacks re-applied dedicated ladder credits totaling $12,360 provisional. Finance notified and provisional invoice adjusted; customer issued a pro forma credit and payment hold released. Long-term fix: patch in rateservice to validate tenant->plan mapping at postback time and fallback-safe tagging, QA review scheduled. Related PRs: rateservice PR #879 contains lookup fix; reconciler PR #412 adds idempotent reprocessing. Follow-up action: postmortem and alert rule to detect mismatch between reserved-tagged requests and billing ladder mappings.
